neighbours.label: a time period named as ending or leading up to something: 'end of the Cretaceous', 'pre-war', 'the years leading up to', 'late Medieval era'
fire: The mammoths vanished near the end of the last Ice Age.
In the pre-war decade the factory doubled its output.
In the months leading up to the election, prices soared.
Ammonites thrived until the close of the Cretaceous.
Trade collapsed toward the end of the Roman era.
The town grew rapidly in the late Victorian period.
In the years leading up to the revolution, bread was scarce.
Ferns covered the land during the late Jurassic.
quiet: The mammoths were hunted by people on the open plains.
In the last decade the factory doubled its output.
In the months after the election, prices fell.
Ammonites had spiral shells divided into chambers.
Trade collapsed when the harbour silted up.
The town grew rapidly once the railway arrived.
In the years after the revolution, bread was cheap.
Ferns covered the forest floor near the stream.

notes: probe: 'end of the Cretaceous' 0.62 (on 'ret'), 'pre-war' 0.26; '1930s' 0.09 and 'Medieval era' 0.01 weak. Output (- pole) promotes 'until/before/pre'.
